title: LATER-PERIOD DISBURSEMENT, STRICTLY INSIDE REPAYMENT PERIOD 3. The same loan as LSCAP-DISB-P1 disbursed 2024-04-10 -- inside period 3's window 2024-04-01..2024-05-01, several periods after the first due date. The oracle emits all-zero REPAYMENT rows 1, 2 and 3 FIRST, then the DISBURSEMENT row dated 2024-04-10, then repayments 4..6. A deeper later-period instance of the emi.go:1529 non-first arm than P1.
_note: TRANSCRIPTION NOTES. (1) request.currency.code is 'MNT'; admit.go requires upper case, and the capture already spells it so. (2) request.time_zone is DECLARED, not observed: the Path A embeddable seam takes java.time.LocalDate only and has no time-zone input at all (the capture JVM ran with defaultTimeZone GMT), so Asia/Ulaanbaatar is this vector's declared interpretation zone for civil dates and grades nothing. (3) request.rounding.rate_factor_scale is 19 from PIN.json's production_rounding; the capture records one MathContext precision (19) which is both. (4) On the DISBURSEMENT row, installment_number and interest_minor are marked unrecorded_fields: the oracle's own record type LoanSchedulePlanDisbursementPeriod carries exactly four fields (periodFromDate, periodDueDate, principalAmount, outstandingLoanBalance), its periodNumber() returns null, and it has no interest accessor; Capture3j.java emits every field the record does carry. DEC-1 normalises the null installment number to 0 and that normalisation is part of the CONTRACT, not an oracle observation -- filling it here would be storing a derivation as an observation. (5) The capture's per-row totalOutstandingBalance column is deliberately NOT promoted: it is principal plus interest still to accrue, not an outstanding-principal figure, and the frozen contract has no field for it. (6) The all-zero REPAYMENT rows before the disbursement carry the oracle's own principal/interest/balance 0.00; their observed_total_due_minor is the capture's total 0.00.

graded_against.description: Emits the level installment in the final period like every other period, so the final principal is (installment - interest) instead of the WHOLE REMAINING BALANCE. The schedule then does not amortize to exactly zero.
graded_against.evidence: Derived at (19, HALF_UP) from cells observed in this capture. Observed level installment (row total on every non-final paying period) = 341568.92; observed FINAL row total = 341568.91, so the oracle does NOT carry the level installment into the final period. Counterfactual final principal = level installment 341568.92 - observed final interest 1980.93 = 339587.99. Observed final principal = 339587.98. Margin = |33958798 - 33958799| = 1 minor units, and the counterfactual's closing balance is non-zero, so the principal_amortizes_to_zero invariant also catches it.

graded_against.description: Splits the principal evenly across the repayments (principal / n each period) and adds declining-balance interest on top, instead of taking principal as the BALANCING REMAINDER of a level installment after interest. Produces a rising total due rather than a level one.
graded_against.evidence: Derived at (19, HALF_UP). Counterfactual per-period principal = disbursed 1014632.37 / 6 = 169105.40 (HALF_UP to 2dp). Widest disagreement is at paying period 3 of the non-zero rows, where the oracle OBSERVED principal 339587.98 (33958798 minor units) against the counterfactual's 169105.40 (16910540 minor units): margin = 17048258 minor units. The disbursed amount and every observed principal are transcribed from this capture; only the division is derived.
